minutes.headline: Planning Board continued three hearings to August 9 and 23 and voted to post the Howard Street workshop; no approvals.
minutes.summary: With two members absent, the board continued the 7-Eleven, 360 Flat Hill Road and 101 Pleasant Street hearings. The main discussion was 101 Pleasant Street, where the board worried that retaining walls in the right-of-way could become the town's burden if the road is later accepted. The board also approved minutes, heard committee reports and decided to post the August 3 Howard Street workshop as a meeting.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at the start; none offered in the room or on Zoom.

A caller with an interest in the Pleasant Street property wanted to comment after the hearing was continued; he shared concern about a waiver being a self-induced hardship and said he would email thoughts to the planner.

Applicant's side to talk to DPW and conservation about the retaining walls before the August 9 hearing.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board continued the 101 Pleasant Street subdivision hearing to August 9 after a long discussion of retaining walls in the right-of-way.
The board continued the 360 Flat Hill Road scenic road hearing to August 23, by a vote of 3-0.
The board continued the 7-Eleven Mass Ave hearing to August 9; no project was approved at this meeting.
The board agreed to post the August 3 Howard Street workshop as a meeting, so it can deliberate if a quorum attends.
The board plans to finalize a single comment letter on the Howard Street project on August 9, for the town manager on August 10.

why_it_matters: At 101 Pleasant Street, the board's concern was that walls in the right-of-way could become a maintenance cost to the town if the road is later accepted as a public way.
The Howard Street comment letter is the board's formal input on a project in town, and the August 3 workshop is a posted meeting residents can attend.
